This bulletin implements the nonfunctional turf prohibition enacted by the Nevada Legislature in Assembly Bill

cooperation with its member agencies. Assembly Bill 356 directs the removal of nonfunctional turf from
properties served by the Colorado River Commission of Nevada and, by extension, from properties served by
SNWA member agencies.
The compliance deadline for the removal or conversion of all nonfunctional turf on properties subject to the
prohibition is 12/31/2026. On and after that date, the presence of nonfunctional turf on a property subject to the
prohibition constitutes a continuing violation of the state statute and of the water service rules of the SNWA
member agencies.


Homeowner association (HOA) owned or managed common-area property, including entry features,
streetscape strips, medians, park parcels, tot lots, and greenbelts;

Commercial, industrial, mixed-use, institutional, and multi-family residential properties;

Governmental, quasi-governmental, and school-district properties;

Vacant parcels held for future development on which existing turf remains irrigated.
Property owners and their agents are directed to identify all turf areas on affected properties, to classify each
area as functional or nonfunctional under the definitions set out in Section 3, and to schedule conversion of
nonfunctional areas so that removal is complete on or before the deadline.
2. Single-Family Residential Carve-Out
The nonfunctional turf prohibition does not apply to turf located within an individually-owned single-family
residential lot. Turf inside the recorded boundary of a single-family residential lot — front yard, side yard, back
yard, and any other area within the four corners of the lot as recorded — is exempt from the mandate
established by AB 356 and this bulletin. Owners of single-family residential lots remain subject to the general
water-waste ordinances and outdoor-watering restrictions of their retail purveyor but are not required by AB
356 to remove existing turf.
The single-family residential carve-out is lot-based, not project-based. The following areas are outside the
carve-out and remain fully subject to the prohibition even where they lie within a subdivision the zoning of

Turf that lies outside the single-family residential carve-out is subject to the prohibition unless it qualifies under
one of the functional categories set out below. Each category has a specific qualifying test. Turf that does not
satisfy the test for one of these categories is nonfunctional turf and must be converted on or before the deadline.

Definition. Grass located within a designated play area containing playground amenities including slides,
swings, and climbing structures, on homeowner association owned or managed common-area property.
Qualifying test. All of the following must be present:
1.
The turf lies within a designated play area — that is, an area drawn on approved landscape plans, or
established on the ground by fencing, borders, or other physical delineation, and identified as a play area
intended for use by children.
2.
The designated play area contains installed and operable playground amenities of the character enumerated
above — specifically, slides, swings, and climbing structures. A designated play area lacking installed
playground amenities does not qualify as playground turf, regardless of the sign or plan label attached to
the area.
3.
The turf lies on property owned or managed by a homeowner association, or by a comparable body
responsible for the common-area landscape.
Turf lying outside the boundary of the designated play area — even in the same park parcel, and even if
visually continuous with the qualifying turf — does not fall within this category and must be classified
independently.

2.
The shortest dimension of that contiguous area, measured perpendicular to its longest dimension, is not

3.
The area is used, or is dedicated to be used, for organized athletic activity — organized team sports,
physical education, formal recreation league play, or similar use. General passive lawn use, decorative
lawn, and informal recreation do not satisfy this element.

not recognized under this category and should not be relied on to justify continued irrigation of common-area

Waiver of the removal requirement is available in narrow circumstances, and only where the application
demonstrates that the turf in question substantially complies with the functional turf definition for one of the

A dimensioned exhibit showing the turf area and the elements relied upon to establish functional character

playground amenities; for athletic field turf, the contiguous area with dimensions and evidence of organized
use);

A written statement identifying the functional category asserted and addressing each element of that
category's qualifying test;

the functional use will be maintained after the compliance deadline.

available for turf that does not meet a functional category. In particular:

waived under Section 3.2 by asserting occasional recreational use; the organized-athletic-activity element is

application and may be combined with, but do not substitute for, the qualifying test.

violation. SNWA and its member agencies will exercise the following enforcement mechanisms, singly or in
combination:

Notice of Violation. A written notice identifying the property, the noncompliant turf area, and a cure
period.
2.
Excess-Use Water Rates. Application of the member agency's excess-use rate schedule to the account
serving the property, retroactive to the deadline where the violation is continuing.
3.
Water Waste Fees. Assessment of water waste fees under the member agency's schedule for continued
irrigation of nonfunctional turf.
4.

flow restrictor on the service and, ultimately, discontinuation of water service in accordance with the
member agency's service rules and Nevada law.

 Contiguous. Forming a single, connected turf surface, uninterrupted by pavement, planter, structure, or

### Project Engineering & Entitlement Review: Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3
**Sundial Job No.:** 2201-03 | **County Applications:** IP-26-100288 & FM-26-100290 | **Tentative Map:** TM-22-500041  
**Anchor Date:** October 31, 2026  

---

### Executive Determination: Can We Commit to the 11/30/2026 Resubmittal Date?

1. **Unconditional Commitment:** **NO.** We cannot make an unconditional commitment to resubmit on November 30, 2026, under Garrett Nokes’s assumption that Clark County Public Works Comment L-4 (and Comment L-2) can be treated as routine "clerical redlines." Adding **150 street trees (+258%)** across 4,160 linear feet of dedicated right-of-way represents a major physical replatting and hydraulic recalculation that directly impacts dry utility joint-trench clearances, sight visibility triangles, sidewalk root barrier assemblies, annual water budget allocations, and performance bonding.
2. **Conditional Commitment:** **YES, WE CAN COMMIT TO 11/30/2026**, but **ONLY IF** Callaway Land Partners and the design team take immediate, decisive action to clear three external blockers during the first week of November (no later than **Friday, November 6, 2026**):
   - **Prerequisite 1 (Park Turf Scope Direction):** Callaway must abandon the legally invalid "single-family residential carve-out" position for the Parcel A common-area park (which directly violates Southern Nevada Water Authority [SNWA] Compliance Bulletin WRC-2024-07 Section 2) and formally instruct Ocotillo Landscape Studio to either **reintroduce playground amenities** on Sheet L-3 (qualifying the lawn as functional playground turf under SNWA Section 3.1) or **convert the 18,400 sq. ft. of turf to desert landscape** ahead of the 12/31/2026 AB 356 deadline.
   - **Prerequisite 2 (Comprehensive Planning Condition 14 Concurrence):** Secure written confirmation from Clark County Comprehensive Planning (Odette Marchetti) that neither the street tree density correction nor the park turf resolution constitutes a "significant change" requiring a public hearing Design Review before the Enterprise Town Advisory Board (TAB) and Planning Commission under Tentative Map Condition 14.
   - **Prerequisite 3 (CCWRD Sewer Capacity Confirmation Renewal):** Immediately re-up Clark County Water Reclamation District (CCWRD) capacity confirmation CCWRD-SCC-2025-1187, which **expired on September 30, 2026**. Improvement plans cannot be approved by Public Works with an expired sewer capacity letter.
3. **Existential Statutory Warning (NRS 278.360):** Title Officer Neil Petrosyan’s email of 10/26/2026 advising that the tentative map is protected through March 2028 is **factually and legally incorrect**. Because Phase 3 is a *successive final map* in a phased series, under NRS 278.360 and TM-22-500041 Conditions of Approval, it must be presented within two (2) years of the recordation of Phases 1 & 2 (recorded December 23, 2024). **The true statutory presentation deadline is DECEMBER 23, 2026.** Failure to present a recordable final map by December 23, 2026, terminates the tentative map by operation of law. With Public Works requiring up to 20 business days for second-round review, any flawed resubmittal that triggers round-three comments will cause the entitlement to lapse.

---

### Key Technical Findings: Comment L-4 vs. Current Landscape Sheets & Tracker

- **Frontage & Tree Density (Title 30 sec. 30.64.030(k)):**
  - **Windmill Lane (North Frontage):** 2,560 LF @ 1 tree / 20 LF = **128 trees required** (currently 34 shown; **deficit of 94 trees**).
  - **Phase 3 Interior Collector:** 1,180 LF @ 1 tree / 20 LF = **59 trees required** (currently 16 shown; **deficit of 43 trees**).
  - **Rainbow Boulevard (East Entry):** 420 LF @ 1 tree / 20 LF = **21 trees required** (currently 8 shown; **deficit of 13 trees**).
  - **Total Phase 3 Street Frontage:** 4,160 LF = **208 trees required vs. 58 trees shown** (**Net deficit of 150 trees**).
- **Physical Siting & Multi-Discipline Clash Constraints:**
  - *Dry Utility Joint Trench (Comments U-1, U-5, Advisory A-1):* General Note 12 on Sheet L-1 prohibits planting trees within dedicated utility easements without written utility joinder. Siting 150 additional trees requires strict clash detection against the dry utility composite plan (conduits, gas mains, 6 pad-mounted transformers, 30 handholes/pull boxes, and 24 streetlight foundations).
  - *Sight Visibility Triangles (Title 30 sec. 30.52.025 / Condition 6):* 30' $\times$ 30' sight zones at intersections and driveways (notably Rainbow Blvd. / Interior Collector per Sheet L-4) must remain clear of vegetation over 24" in height.
  - *Sidewalk Linear Root Barriers (Detail 6 / Sheet L-1):* 10-ft modular panels (24" deep) are required at all street trees adjacent to public sidewalks, adding **1,500 LF of root barrier assemblies**.
  - *Shade Coverage Guidance (CP-PW-GM-2025-04):* A formal Shade Coverage Exhibit must be provided demonstrating 30% 15-year canopy coverage.
- **Irrigation Demand & Water Budget Impacts:**
  - Applying the approved rate of 2,000 gal/tree/year, Phase 3 tree demand increases from **148,000 gal/yr (0.45 ac-ft/yr)** across 74 trees to **448,000 gal/yr (1.38 ac-ft/yr)** across 224 total common-area trees.
  - Net annual irrigation demand increases by **300,000 gal/yr (+0.92 ac-ft/yr)**, driving total Phase 3 common-area demand from **3.28 ac-ft/yr to 4.21 ac-ft/yr (+28.0%)**.
  - Sizing of laterals, remote control valves, and dedicated meters (1½" at Parcel A, ¾" at entry monument) must be verified, and supporting worksheets (`DSR_Irrigation_Demand_Worksheet.xlsx`, `DSR_Ph3_Water_Budget.xlsx`, and `DSR_Ph3_Turf_Planting_Tabulation.xlsx`) must be reissued.
- **Performance Bond Estimate Revision (Advisory A-6 / Condition 8):**
  - Section 6A of `DSR_Ph3_Engineers_Estimate.xlsx` must be revised: Item 7.09 (24" box trees @ $485/EA) increases by +150 EA (+$72,750), Item 7.42 drip emitters increases by +150 EA (+$1,875), plus root barrier allowances (+$6,750).
  - Total bonded estimate increases by **+$83,000**, adjusting the performance bond basis from **$5,357,000.00 to $5,440,000.00**. Callaway’s surety broker must be alerted immediately.
- **Enterprise TAB Bottleneck & Community Protest Risk:**
  - Condition 14 mandates public hearing design review before TAB and Planning Commission for any "significant change."
  - The 11/18/2026 Enterprise TAB application cutoff was **10/28/2026 (expired)**; the next TAB is **12/16/2026** (Planning Commission in January 2027). Any TAB referral makes December recordation impossible.
  - Sagebrook Community Management’s letter of 10/17/2026 confirmed that Phase 1/2 homeowners are attending the 11/18 TAB meeting to protest Callaway’s VE cut of the Phase 3 park playground amenities, threatening to trigger administrative review.

---

The complete analysis, technical exhibits, and formal memorandum have been authored and placed under `output/`:

1. **`output/MEMO_CALLAWAY_L4_LANDSCAPE_RESUBMITTAL_2026-10-31.md`**  
   *Comprehensive, authoritative formal memorandum addressed to Garrett Nokes (Callaway Land Partners), dated October 31, 2026, prepared for the signature of Jonathan R. Kessler, PE (Principal / Engineer of Record, Sundial Engineering & Survey) and countersigned by Max Braddock (Project Manager).* Details the feasibility commitment, Comment L-4 technical evaluation, irrigation recalculations, bond revisions, SNWA turf legal refutation, NRS 278.360 statutory clock correction, Enterprise TAB risks, and the chronological prerequisite roadmap.
2. **`output/MEMO_CALLAWAY_L4_LANDSCAPE_RESUBMITTAL_2026-10-31.docx`**  
   *Professional Microsoft Word (.docx) version of the formal memorandum*, complete with executive typography, navy/slate styling, formatted tables (street frontage calculations and hydrozone water budgets), callout formatting, and signature blocks.
3. **`output/EXHIBIT_A_L4_TECHNICAL_EVALUATION_AND_IRRIGATION_IMPACTS.md`**  
   *Technical engineering exhibit* detailing linear frontage breakdowns, species allocation on Sheet L-1, comparative water budget tables (current vs. revised demand), performance bond line-item adjustments, and multi-discipline spatial clash detection hold-lines (dry utilities, sight triangles, and hydrants).
4. **`output/EXHIBIT_B_RESUBMITTAL_PREREQUISITES_AND_CRITICAL_PATH.md`**  
   *Comprehensive critical path and tracking exhibit* reconciling all 10 Outstanding Items from the Resubmittal Tracker, analyzing the NRS 278.360 statutory successive map presentation clock, and establishing a day-by-day milestone schedule from October 31, 2026, through November 30 resubmittal and December 23 statutory map presentation.
